items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (e.g. 9/12/2025 and 6/22/2026). No anticoagulant is current: the only active clinic prescriptions are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin; the DOACs she received (dabigatran/rivaroxaban/apixaban) ended with the January 2025 admission. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (age >=75 = 2, female = 1, hypertension, heart failure, diabetes, prior cerebral infarction = 2, coronary/vascular disease), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. Aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily has been continuous since 5/14/2024 and is current (order 7/18/2026, valid to 12/26/2026). The most recent ECG in the chart (10/8/2023, record 108018814) shows sinus rhythm at 68-70 bpm with QT about 492 ms and Bazett QTc about 524 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT memo, despite the 5/14/2024 note describing that tracing as 'QT acceptable'. Latest electrolytes 3/18/2026: K 3.8 mEq/L, Mg 1.9 mg/dL. Prescriber review (and a current ECG) is required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (twice the dose recommended above age 60 in other guidance, and a QT watch-list drug) is current - order 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027. Her most recent ECG, 11/10/2023 (record 104821039), shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT about 487 ms and Bazett QTc about 527 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which requires prescriber review under the clinic QT memo. Most recent electrolytes: K 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and Mg 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025).

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025. Because the start was on or after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days (by 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met - although that tracing shows QTc ~549 ms and is the basis of a separate QT safety item.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days (by 3/16/2026). ECG 104882441 was obtained on 3/7/2026, five days after the start, and shows sinus rhythm with QTc ~370 ms, so the requirement was completed in time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (ECG due by 3/14/2026). ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start (QTc ~460 ms), so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026, i.e. after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days - by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded on 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start, so the requirement was not met within the required time and remains outstanding past its due date. Escitalopram has been continued (current order 8/11/2026); the 4/29/2026 tracing itself showed QTc ~377 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days (by 8/24/2026). No ECG exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested by fax and not yet received. That outside tracing, if obtained on 8/18/2026, would have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started (re-started as an outpatient, the December 2025 order having been an inpatient course) at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days - by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, well before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since; the requirement is overdue as of the evaluation date.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been recorded since 3/9/2025, but the window has not closed as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation, so the requirement is not yet due; it should be arranged in the next five days.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 9/1/2026 the physician documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the follow-up requirement was completed on time.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded 8/22/2025 and carried in every cardiology clinic note). Current medications are levothyroxine only - no anticoagulant and no antiplatelet; no anticoagulant order has ever been written. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1, coronary atherosclerosis/vascular disease = 1), which is well above the threshold at which the 2023 AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. The 2025 procedure-related haemorrhage was a single peri-procedural event and is not documented as an ongoing contraindication.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (acting under the clinic standing order, which permits pharmacist dose adjustment) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. The 3/1/2026 memo requires a clinic INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026 and no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the required follow-up is overdue in a 95-year-old on amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin.

48-year-old man whose cardiology clinic notes consistently list paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (most recently 8/4/2026). Warfarin/heparin were given only during the February and June 2025 admissions; current clinic medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline, so no anticoagulant is current. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure documented 2/26/2025 and hypertension), and with a score of >=2 in a man the guideline recommends oral anticoagulation.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the March 2025 admission for embolic cerebral infarction. Current clinic medications are famotidine, metoprolol and levothyroxine - rate control only, with no anticoagulant on the list at any visit since (last visit 6/2/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (prior cerebral infarction = 2, age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1, female = 1). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention; documented falls and thrombocytopenia should be weighed but are not an absolute contraindication.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 8/20/2026 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nevertheless listed as a current medication and re-prescribed (order 8/20/2026, valid to 1/4/2027), together with aspirin and clopidogrel. Restarting a DOAC plus dual antiplatelet therapy after a recent major GI bleed has not been reconciled with the documented hold and requires prescriber review.

At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-issued the same day (valid to 1/3/2027) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid to 12/23/2026), and the note's medication list contains both. Both orders are still current on 9/24/2026, so the patient is prescribed two oral anticoagulants simultaneously (plus clopidogrel) - a bleeding hazard that needs immediate reconciliation.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (17:13 record 107914094 and 19:36 record 103088543) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at about 135-145 bpm with no organised P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and atrial fibrillation was coded at that encounter. The rhythm statement in the note is contradicted by the same-day tracings and should be corrected.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is current (re-ordered 7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027). His most recent ECG, 11/24/2025, shows sinus rhythm at 62-64 bpm with QT about 540 ms and Bazett QTc about 549 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which under the clinic QT monitoring memo requires prescriber review. Electrolytes are not contributory (K 4.3 mEq/L and Mg 2.1 mg/dL on 6/9/2026). No repeat ECG has been obtained since amiodarone was continued.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027) and warfarin. Her most recent ECG in the chart (4/27/2022, record 101515306) shows atrial fibrillation at about 74-77 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT (~555-580 ms, Bazett QTc ~616-640 ms), far above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT memo, so prescriber review is required. Latest electrolytes 6/17/2026: K 4.2 mEq/L, Mg 1.9 mg/dL. A current ECG should be obtained as part of that review.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with an upright, uniform P wave before every QRS (P-R 182 ms). Narrow QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about +47 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 319 ms, Bazett QTc 370 ms - normal despite citalopram 40 mg daily. No earlier ECG is available for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at about 104 bpm, regular, with a low-amplitude P wave and P-R 120 ms. QRS 92 ms, axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 366 ms, Bazett QTc 480 ms (upper normal). Compared with 6/20/2025 (sinus tachycardia 147 bpm, P-R 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 434 ms) the rate has fallen; there is no new arrhythmia or block and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at about 108 bpm with a P wave before every QRS, P-R 114 ms, QRS 88 ms, frontal axis +36 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 343 ms, Bazett QTc 463 ms (borderline but below 500 ms). Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR (348-650 ms), mean rate about 136 bpm, no organised P waves (only a negative baseline undulation in lead II), so no measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, axis about 0 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 282 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms. The ECG two hours earlier the same day (107914094) shows the same atrial fibrillation at 134 bpm with QTc 439 ms, so nothing has changed between them - but both contradict the 6/10/2026 note describing sinus rhythm at 72 (see contradiction item).

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at about 69-72 bpm (RR 864-882 ms) with no P wave visible in any lead on beat-by-beat or signal-averaged review, only a small negative deflection in lead II - an accelerated junctional / low atrial rhythm rather than sinus, and no PR interval can be measured. One late premature beat. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about -24 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 405 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 also lacked sinus P waves (rate 61, QTc about 401 ms), so the rhythm and intervals are unchanged; note that tracing also showed a reversed limb-lead pattern.

Sinus rhythm at about 98 bpm, regular, P-R 110 ms, QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about +4 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 301 ms, Bazett QTc 384 ms. Single ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at about 72 bpm with a constant upright P wave, P-R 142 ms, QRS 76 ms, axis +22 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave ends early (peak ~270 ms): QT about 376 ms, Bazett QTc about 412 ms - normal. Only ECG in the chart; it predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026, so it cannot serve as the post-start tracing (see follow-up item).

Atrial fibrillation: grossly irregular RR intervals (462-1154 ms), mean ventricular rate about 70 bpm, no consistent P waves, so no PR interval. QRS 78 ms, axis +27 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 421 ms with Bazett QTc about 491 ms. Three days earlier (11/12/2024, record 107873952) the rhythm was regular sinus at 69 bpm with clear P waves (P-R 166 ms) and QTc 398 ms, so this tracing shows new atrial fibrillation and a QTc rise of more than 60 ms. She is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus bradycardia at about 58 bpm with prominent upright P waves, P-R 106 ms, QRS 80 ms, axis +62 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 420 ms, Bazett QTc 414 ms. Essentially identical to the tracing of the previous day (106045460: 62 bpm, P-R 110 ms, QTc 440 ms) - no rhythm, conduction or QTc change. This is the baseline against which the ECG now due after the 9/15/2026 haloperidol start should be compared.
Sinus rhythm at about 83 bpm, very regular, P-R 140 ms, QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 346 ms, Bazett QTc 407 ms. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at about 76 bpm with large upright P waves, P-R 152 ms, QRS 66 ms, axis +64 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 399 ms, Bazett QTc 451 ms. Compared with 2/2/2020 (sinus 75 bpm, P-R 150 ms, QTc about 499 ms) the QTc is slightly shorter (change under 60 ms) and there is no new arrhythmia or block.

Sinus tachycardia at about 120 bpm with consistent P waves, P-R 178 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis +51 degrees, no conduction block. QT 274 ms, QTc 388 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus at 108 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 393 ms) there is no significant change: no new arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and QTc differs by only 5 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at about 55 bpm (RR 1074-1118 ms). Each QRS is preceded by a broad upright P wave with a prolonged P-R of about 216-230 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms with prominent septal q waves, frontal axis about 0 to +60 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 396 ms, Bazett QTc 377 ms. The prior ECG of 11/30/2024 showed sinus rhythm with frequent bigeminal ectopy, P-R about 190 ms and QTc about 411 ms; the rhythm is still sinus, there is no new bundle branch block and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR (316-602 ms), mean rate about 147 bpm, no organised atrial activity and no measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about -21 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 260 ms, Bazett QTc 413 ms. The tracing of the previous evening (107374881) was also irregular without consistent P waves at a slower rate (about 84 bpm), so atrial fibrillation is not new between these two; he is on apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at about 72 bpm with a well-formed upright P wave, P-R 166 ms, QRS 86 ms (narrow - the apparent widening on automated review was baseline offset), frontal axis about +12 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 353 ms and Bazett QTc about 391 ms. On 11/21/2025 the T wave was much later (peak 385 ms) with QT about 481 ms and QTc about 512 ms, so the QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms; the rhythm remains sinus, consistent with the 11/23/2025 note.

Sinus rhythm at about 74-75 bpm with a uniform upright P wave, P-R 182 ms (upper normal), QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 372 ms, Bazett QTc 413 ms. One late ectopic beat. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at about 112 bpm, regular (RR 536-542 ms), with a P wave before every QRS and P-R 168 ms. QRS 76 ms, frontal axis +34 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 283 ms, Bazett QTc 386 ms. The prior ECG of 7/4/2022 was also sinus at 115 bpm with P-R 160 ms and QTc 389 ms - unchanged. Note this 2023 tracing is the most recent available even though atrial flutter was coded in 9/2025, and he remains on apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at about 62-63 bpm with an upright P wave before each conducted QRS (P-R about 198 ms, borderline) interrupted by one premature beat and a compensatory pause; no atrial fibrillation is present on this tracing. QRS 98 ms, frontal axis about -30 degrees, reported as left axis deviation (lead I positive, lead II nearly isoelectric, III and aVF negative). No bundle branch block. QT 390 ms, Bazett QTc 397 ms. Only ECG in the chart - her paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented by diagnosis, not on this recording.

Regular rhythm at about 70 bpm with a consistent atrial deflection before every QRS (P-R 144 ms) - sinus in origin, but recorded with a reversed limb-lead pattern: P and QRS are inverted in leads I and II with a positive aVR, giving a measured frontal axis of about -173 degrees (extreme axis deviation), while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block. QT 350 ms, Bazett QTc 377 ms - normal on escitalopram. Only ECG in the chart; it was obtained 19 days after the escitalopram start (see follow-up item).

Sinus rhythm at about 70 bpm, P-R 164 ms, QRS 90 ms, frontal axis +40 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is late and broad (peak ~365 ms) giving QT about 487 ms and Bazett QTc about 527 ms - prolonged. The prior ECG of 6/17/2020 (sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, QTc about 448 ms) shows an increase in QTc of more than 60 ms. She remains on citalopram 40 mg daily (see QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at about 68 bpm with a uniform upright P wave, P-R 146 ms, QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +33 to +66 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. T waves are inverted in leads I and V2 with a slow return to baseline; QT about 434 ms giving Bazett QTc about 463 ms - borderline but below 500 ms. Only ECG in the chart; it satisfies the ECG required after the 2/12/2026 escitalopram start.

Sinus rhythm with frequent premature atrial complexes producing alternating long and short cycles (RR 416-1168 ms, mean rate about 66 bpm); every QRS is preceded by an upright P wave in lead II with P-R about 176 ms, so the rhythm is not atrial fibrillation. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about -5 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 378 ms, Bazett QTc about 358-397 ms depending on the cycle used. The prior ECG of 12/13/2018 was regular sinus at 66 bpm with P-R 200 ms and QTc about 386 ms - no new arrhythmia, block or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at about 70 bpm, P-R 128 ms, QRS 86 ms, axis +45 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is markedly late (T peak ~375 ms) giving QT about 492 ms and Bazett QTc about 524 ms - prolonged. The previous ECG of 11/23/2022 had QTc 347 ms, so QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. Relevant because escitalopram has been taken continuously since 5/2024 (see QT safety item).

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 141 bpm (RR 404-454 ms). Signal-averaged analysis of the inter-QRS segments shows organised atrial activity at about 282 per minute - exactly twice the ventricular rate - with two identical atrial deflections per cycle in leads II, III and V1, i.e. atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction; no true PR interval can be assigned. QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +1 degree, no bundle branch block. QT 271 ms, Bazett QTc 416 ms. The prior ECG of 7/11/2022 showed irregularly irregular atrial fibrillation at about 107 bpm, so the organised flutter is new and the fibrillation has resolved; atrial flutter was coded at this admission. QTc is unchanged (431 to 416 ms).

Sinus rhythm at about 82 bpm, regular, with a clear upright P wave, P-R 158 ms, QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about +34 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 370 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at about 91 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II beginning about 210 ms before the QRS (P-R about 175 ms, within normal limits once the depressed PR segment is excluded), QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about -17 to +45 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms. The prior ECG of 5/16/2021 was sinus at 87 bpm with P-R 142 ms and QTc 390 ms - no new arrhythmia, conduction block or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at about 59-61 bpm. The P wave precedes each QRS with a prolonged P-R of about 216-235 ms (first-degree AV block). QRS duration is 120 ms with a left bundle branch block pattern - rS/QS in V1-V2, broad monophasic R in I and V6 with delayed R-peak time (about 65 ms) and absent septal q. Frontal axis about -21 degrees (normal). QT 442 ms, Bazett QTc 446 ms. The prior ECG of 6/3/2024 shows the identical picture (P-R 212 ms, QRS 120 ms, QTc 446 ms), so the AV block and bundle branch block are not new and the QTc is unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at about 102 bpm, regular, P-R 132 ms, QRS 88 ms, frontal axis +45 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 432 ms. The tracing from the previous day (101016166) is essentially the same (101 bpm, P-R 128 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 424 ms): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at about 66-72 bpm with a constant upright P wave (P-R 152 ms) before every sinus beat, interrupted by two premature ventricular complexes late in the strip; the underlying rhythm is regular, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about -20 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 370 ms, Bazett QTc 388 ms. Only ECG in the chart.

Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (406-1084 ms, mean rate about 77 bpm) with no consistent P waves, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 76 ms, frontal axis +36 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is very broad and late (peak about 420 ms): QT about 555-580 ms and Bazett QTc about 616-640 ms, markedly prolonged. The prior ECG of 4/6/2022 was also atrial fibrillation (rate about 128 bpm) but with QTc about 426 ms, so the QTc has increased by far more than 60 ms - she is on amiodarone (see QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia at about 107 bpm, regular, with a P wave before each QRS and P-R 158 ms. QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +52 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 324 ms, Bazett QTc 433 ms. Compared with 7/27/2019 (sinus 75 bpm, P-R 150 ms, QTc about 424 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no new block and no significant QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 492-500 ms), with a P wave before each QRS and P-R 138 ms. QRS is narrow (58 ms), frontal axis +69 degrees (normal), no conduction abnormality. QT 277 ms with Bazett QTc 392 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at about 102 bpm, P-R 152 ms, QRS 70 ms, axis +59 degrees, no bundle branch block, QT 308 ms and QTc 400 ms. The comparison tracing was taken one minute earlier the same day (8/23/2021) and is essentially identical (rate 100, P-R 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QTc 397 ms): no interval or rhythm change.

Sinus bradycardia at about 52 bpm (RR 1145-1180 ms) with a uniform upright P wave before every QRS, P-R 180 ms (upper normal), QRS 68 ms, axis +36 degrees, no block. QT 413 ms, QTc 384 ms. Versus 5/22/2023 (sinus at 58 bpm with occasional ectopy, P-R 148 ms, QTc 379 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and no significant QTc change; the patient remains in sinus rhythm on warfarin for atrial fibrillation.

Sinus tachycardia at about 122 bpm, P-R 126 ms, QRS 102 ms with only a small terminal r' in V1 (incomplete right bundle pattern, duration below 120 ms). Frontal axis about +135 degrees - right axis deviation (S dominant in lead I, positive in III/aVF). QT 293 ms, QTc 416 ms. The earlier tracing from the same day (1:33, record 106516875) showed complete right bundle branch block with QRS 144 ms and a broad terminal R in V1; the QRS has narrowed to 102 ms, i.e. the bundle branch block has resolved. QTc is essentially unchanged (462 to 416 ms).

Sinus rhythm at about 62-64 bpm with a low-amplitude but constant P wave (P-R 170 ms) and one late ectopic beat. QRS 90 ms, axis +66 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is broad and late (peak ~410 ms): QT about 540 ms and Bazett QTc about 549 ms, markedly prolonged on amiodarone started 11/10/2025. The prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (sinus with marked pauses, QTc about 438 ms) shows the QTc has risen by more than 100 ms - see the QT safety item.

Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR 408-726 ms) with no discernible P wave in any lead, only low-amplitude fibrillatory activity, so no PR interval can be measured. Mean ventricular rate about 109 bpm. QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about -47 degrees (left axis deviation), no bundle branch block. QT 313 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart; the patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days (by 8/24/2026). Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started (re-started as an outpatient, the December 2025 order having been an inpatient course) at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days - by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, well before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since; the requirement is overdue as of the evaluation date.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been recorded since 3/9/2025, but the window has not closed as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation, so the requirement is not yet due; it should be arranged in the next five days.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 9/1/2026 the physician documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the follow-up requirement was completed on time.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded 8/22/2025 and carried in every cardiology clinic note). Current medications are levothyroxine only - no anticoagulant and no antiplatelet; no anticoagulant order has ever been written. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1, coronary atherosclerosis/vascular disease = 1), which is well above the threshold at which the 2023 AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. The 2025 procedure-related haemorrhage was a single peri-procedural event and is not documented as an ongoing contraindication.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (acting under the clinic standing order, which permits pharmacist dose adjustment) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. The 3/1/2026 memo requires a clinic INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026 and no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the required follow-up is overdue in a 95-year-old on amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin.

48-year-old man whose cardiology clinic notes consistently list paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (most recently 8/4/2026). Warfarin/heparin were given only during the February and June 2025 admissions; current clinic medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline, so no anticoagulant is current. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure documented 2/26/2025 and hypertension), and with a score of >=2 in a man the guideline recommends oral anticoagulation.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the March 2025 admission for embolic cerebral infarction. Current clinic medications are famotidine, metoprolol and levothyroxine - rate control only, with no anticoagulant on the list at any visit since (last visit 6/2/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (prior cerebral infarction = 2, age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1, female = 1). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention; documented falls and thrombocytopenia should be weighed but are not an absolute contraindication.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 8/20/2026 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nevertheless listed as a current medication and re-prescribed (order 8/20/2026, valid to 1/4/2027), together with aspirin and clopidogrel. Restarting a DOAC plus dual antiplatelet therapy after a recent major GI bleed has not been reconciled with the documented hold and requires prescriber review.

At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-issued the same day (valid to 1/3/2027) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid to 12/23/2026), and the note's medication list contains both. Both orders are still current on 9/24/2026, so the patient is prescribed two oral anticoagulants simultaneously (plus clopidogrel) - a bleeding hazard that needs immediate reconciliation.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (17:13 record 107914094 and 19:36 record 103088543) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at about 135-145 bpm with no organised P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and atrial fibrillation was coded at that encounter. The rhythm statement in the note is contradicted by the same-day tracings and should be corrected.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is current (re-ordered 7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027). His most recent ECG, 11/24/2025, shows sinus rhythm at 62-64 bpm with QT about 540 ms and Bazett QTc about 549 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which under the clinic QT monitoring memo requires prescriber review. Electrolytes are not contributory (K 4.3 mEq/L and Mg 2.1 mg/dL on 6/9/2026). No repeat ECG has been obtained since amiodarone was continued.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027) and warfarin. Her most recent ECG in the chart (4/27/2022, record 101515306) shows atrial fibrillation at about 74-77 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT (~555-580 ms, Bazett QTc ~616-640 ms), far above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT memo, so prescriber review is required. Latest electrolytes 6/17/2026: K 4.2 mEq/L, Mg 1.9 mg/dL. A current ECG should be obtained as part of that review.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with an upright, uniform P wave before every QRS (P-R 182 ms). Narrow QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about +47 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 319 ms, Bazett QTc 370 ms - normal despite citalopram 40 mg daily. No earlier ECG is available for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at about 104 bpm, regular, with a low-amplitude P wave and P-R 120 ms. QRS 92 ms, axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 366 ms, Bazett QTc 480 ms (upper normal). Compared with 6/20/2025 (sinus tachycardia 147 bpm, P-R 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 434 ms) the rate has fallen; there is no new arrhythmia or block and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at about 108 bpm with a P wave before every QRS, P-R 114 ms, QRS 88 ms, frontal axis +36 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 343 ms, Bazett QTc 463 ms (borderline but below 500 ms). Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR (348-650 ms), mean rate about 136 bpm, no organised P waves (only a negative baseline undulation in lead II), so no measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, axis about 0 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 282 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms. The ECG two hours earlier the same day (107914094) shows the same atrial fibrillation at 134 bpm with QTc 439 ms, so nothing has changed between them - but both contradict the 6/10/2026 note describing sinus rhythm at 72 (see contradiction item).

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at about 69-72 bpm (RR 864-882 ms) with no P wave visible in any lead on beat-by-beat or signal-averaged review, only a small negative deflection in lead II - an accelerated junctional / low atrial rhythm rather than sinus, and no PR interval can be measured. One late premature beat. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about -24 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 405 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 also lacked sinus P waves (rate 61, QTc about 401 ms), so the rhythm and intervals are unchanged; note that tracing also showed a reversed limb-lead pattern.

Sinus rhythm at about 98 bpm, regular, P-R 110 ms, QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about +4 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 301 ms, Bazett QTc 384 ms. Single ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at about 72 bpm with a constant upright P wave, P-R 142 ms, QRS 76 ms, axis +22 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave ends early (peak ~270 ms): QT about 376 ms, Bazett QTc about 412 ms - normal. Only ECG in the chart; it predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026, so it cannot serve as the post-start tracing (see follow-up item).

Atrial fibrillation: grossly irregular RR intervals (462-1154 ms), mean ventricular rate about 70 bpm, no consistent P waves, so no PR interval. QRS 78 ms, axis +27 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 421 ms with Bazett QTc about 491 ms. Three days earlier (11/12/2024, record 107873952) the rhythm was regular sinus at 69 bpm with clear P waves (P-R 166 ms) and QTc 398 ms, so this tracing shows new atrial fibrillation and a QTc rise of more than 60 ms. She is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus bradycardia at about 58 bpm with prominent upright P waves, P-R 106 ms, QRS 80 ms, axis +62 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 420 ms, Bazett QTc 414 ms. Essentially identical to the tracing of the previous day (106045460: 62 bpm, P-R 110 ms, QTc 440 ms) - no rhythm, conduction or QTc change. This is the baseline against which the ECG now due after the 9/15/2026 haloperidol start should be compared.
Sinus rhythm at about 83 bpm, very regular, P-R 140 ms, QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 346 ms, Bazett QTc 407 ms. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at about 76 bpm with large upright P waves, P-R 152 ms, QRS 66 ms, axis +64 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 399 ms, Bazett QTc 451 ms. Compared with 2/2/2020 (sinus 75 bpm, P-R 150 ms, QTc about 499 ms) the QTc is slightly shorter (change under 60 ms) and there is no new arrhythmia or block.

Sinus tachycardia at about 120 bpm with consistent P waves, P-R 178 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis +51 degrees, no conduction block. QT 274 ms, QTc 388 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus at 108 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 393 ms) there is no significant change: no new arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and QTc differs by only 5 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at about 55 bpm (RR 1074-1118 ms). Each QRS is preceded by a broad upright P wave with a prolonged P-R of about 216-230 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms with prominent septal q waves, frontal axis about 0 to +60 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 396 ms, Bazett QTc 377 ms. The prior ECG of 11/30/2024 showed sinus rhythm with frequent bigeminal ectopy, P-R about 190 ms and QTc about 411 ms; the rhythm is still sinus, there is no new bundle branch block and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR (316-602 ms), mean rate about 147 bpm, no organised atrial activity and no measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about -21 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 260 ms, Bazett QTc 413 ms. The tracing of the previous evening (107374881) was also irregular without consistent P waves at a slower rate (about 84 bpm), so atrial fibrillation is not new between these two; he is on apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at about 72 bpm with a well-formed upright P wave, P-R 166 ms, QRS 86 ms (narrow - the apparent widening on automated review was baseline offset), frontal axis about +12 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 353 ms and Bazett QTc about 391 ms. On 11/21/2025 the T wave was much later (peak 385 ms) with QT about 481 ms and QTc about 512 ms, so the QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms; the rhythm remains sinus, consistent with the 11/23/2025 note.

Sinus rhythm at about 74-75 bpm with a uniform upright P wave, P-R 182 ms (upper normal), QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 372 ms, Bazett QTc 413 ms. One late ectopic beat. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at about 112 bpm, regular (RR 536-542 ms), with a P wave before every QRS and P-R 168 ms. QRS 76 ms, frontal axis +34 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 283 ms, Bazett QTc 386 ms. The prior ECG of 7/4/2022 was also sinus at 115 bpm with P-R 160 ms and QTc 389 ms - unchanged. Note this 2023 tracing is the most recent available even though atrial flutter was coded in 9/2025, and he remains on apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at about 62-63 bpm with an upright P wave before each conducted QRS (P-R about 198 ms, borderline) interrupted by one premature beat and a compensatory pause; no atrial fibrillation is present on this tracing. QRS 98 ms, frontal axis about -30 degrees, reported as left axis deviation (lead I positive, lead II nearly isoelectric, III and aVF negative). No bundle branch block. QT 390 ms, Bazett QTc 397 ms. Only ECG in the chart - her paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented by diagnosis, not on this recording.

Regular rhythm at about 70 bpm with a consistent atrial deflection before every QRS (P-R 144 ms) - sinus in origin, but recorded with a reversed limb-lead pattern: P and QRS are inverted in leads I and II with a positive aVR, giving a measured frontal axis of about -173 degrees (extreme axis deviation), while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block. QT 350 ms, Bazett QTc 377 ms - normal on escitalopram. Only ECG in the chart; it was obtained 19 days after the escitalopram start (see follow-up item).

Sinus rhythm at about 70 bpm, P-R 128 ms, QRS 86 ms, axis +45 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is markedly late (T peak ~375 ms) giving QT about 492 ms and Bazett QTc about 524 ms - prolonged. The previous ECG of 11/23/2022 had QTc 347 ms, so QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. Relevant because escitalopram has been taken continuously since 5/2024 (see QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 492-500 ms), with a P wave before each QRS and P-R 138 ms. QRS is narrow (58 ms), frontal axis +69 degrees (normal), no conduction abnormality. QT 277 ms with Bazett QTc 392 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at about 102 bpm, P-R 152 ms, QRS 70 ms, axis +59 degrees, no bundle branch block, QT 308 ms and QTc 400 ms. The comparison tracing was taken one minute earlier the same day (8/23/2021) and is essentially identical (rate 100, P-R 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QTc 397 ms): no interval or rhythm change.

Sinus bradycardia at about 52 bpm (RR 1145-1180 ms) with a uniform upright P wave before every QRS, P-R 180 ms (upper normal), QRS 68 ms, axis +36 degrees, no block. QT 413 ms, QTc 384 ms. Versus 5/22/2023 (sinus at 58 bpm with occasional ectopy, P-R 148 ms, QTc 379 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and no significant QTc change; the patient remains in sinus rhythm on warfarin for atrial fibrillation.

Sinus tachycardia at about 122 bpm, P-R 126 ms, QRS 102 ms with only a small terminal r' in V1 (incomplete right bundle pattern, duration below 120 ms). Frontal axis about +135 degrees - right axis deviation (S dominant in lead I, positive in III/aVF). QT 293 ms, QTc 416 ms. The earlier tracing from the same day (1:33, record 106516875) showed complete right bundle branch block with QRS 144 ms and a broad terminal R in V1; the QRS has narrowed to 102 ms, i.e. the bundle branch block has resolved. QTc is essentially unchanged (462 to 416 ms).

Sinus rhythm at about 62-64 bpm with a low-amplitude but constant P wave (P-R 170 ms) and one late ectopic beat. QRS 90 ms, axis +66 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is broad and late (peak ~410 ms): QT about 540 ms and Bazett QTc about 549 ms, markedly prolonged on amiodarone started 11/10/2025. The prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (sinus with marked pauses, QTc about 438 ms) shows the QTc has risen by more than 100 ms - see the QT safety item.

Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR 408-726 ms) with no discernible P wave in any lead, only low-amplitude fibrillatory activity, so no PR interval can be measured. Mean ventricular rate about 109 bpm. QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about -47 degrees (left axis deviation), no bundle branch block. QT 313 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart; the patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (e.g. 9/12/2025 and 6/22/2026). No anticoagulant is current: the only active clinic prescriptions are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin; the DOACs she received (dabigatran/rivaroxaban/apixaban) ended with the January 2025 admission. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (age >=75 = 2, female = 1, hypertension, heart failure, diabetes, prior cerebral infarction = 2, coronary/vascular disease), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. Aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily has been continuous since 5/14/2024 and is current (order 7/18/2026, valid to 12/26/2026). The most recent ECG in the chart (10/8/2023, record 108018814) shows sinus rhythm at 68-70 bpm with QT about 492 ms and Bazett QTc about 524 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT memo, despite the 5/14/2024 note describing that tracing as 'QT acceptable'. Latest electrolytes 3/18/2026: K 3.8 mEq/L, Mg 1.9 mg/dL. Prescriber review (and a current ECG) is required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (twice the dose recommended above age 60 in other guidance, and a QT watch-list drug) is current - order 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027. Her most recent ECG, 11/10/2023 (record 104821039), shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT about 487 ms and Bazett QTc about 527 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which requires prescriber review under the clinic QT memo. Most recent electrolytes: K 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and Mg 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025).

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025. Because the start was on or after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days (by 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met - although that tracing shows QTc ~549 ms and is the basis of a separate QT safety item.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days (by 3/16/2026). ECG 104882441 was obtained on 3/7/2026, five days after the start, and shows sinus rhythm with QTc ~370 ms, so the requirement was completed in time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (ECG due by 3/14/2026). ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start (QTc ~460 ms), so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026, i.e. after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days - by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded on 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start, so the requirement was not met within the required time and remains outstanding past its due date. Escitalopram has been continued (current order 8/11/2026); the 4/29/2026 tracing itself showed QTc ~377 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days (by 8/24/2026). That outside tracing, if obtained on 8/18/2026, would have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Sinus rhythm at about 104 bpm, regular, with a low-amplitude P wave and P-R 120 ms. QRS 92 ms, axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 366 ms, Bazett QTc 480 ms (upper normal). Compared with 6/20/2025 (sinus tachycardia 147 bpm, P-R 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 434 ms) the rate has fallen; there is no new arrhythmia or block and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 also lacked sinus P waves (rate 61, QTc about 401 ms), so the rhythm and intervals are unchanged; note that tracing also showed a reversed limb-lead pattern.

Sinus rhythm at about 98 bpm, regular, P-R 110 ms, QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about +4 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 301 ms, Bazett QTc 384 ms. Single ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Only ECG in the chart; it predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026, so it cannot serve as the post-start tracing (see follow-up item).

Atrial fibrillation: grossly irregular RR intervals (462-1154 ms), mean ventricular rate about 70 bpm, no consistent P waves, so no PR interval. QRS 78 ms, axis +27 degrees, no bundle branch block. Sinus rhythm at about 83 bpm, very regular, P-R 140 ms, QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 346 ms, Bazett QTc 407 ms. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus bradycardia at about 55 bpm (RR 1074-1118 ms). Each QRS is preceded by a broad upright P wave with a prolonged P-R of about 216-230 ms - first-degree AV block. Sinus rhythm at about 72 bpm with a well-formed upright P wave, P-R 166 ms, QRS 86 ms (narrow - the apparent widening on automated review was baseline offset), frontal axis about +12 degrees, no bundle branch block. Sinus rhythm at about 74-75 bpm with a uniform upright P wave, P-R 182 ms (upper normal), QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 372 ms, Bazett QTc 413 ms. One late ectopic beat. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at about 112 bpm, regular (RR 536-542 ms), with a P wave before every QRS and P-R 168 ms. QRS 76 ms, frontal axis +34 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 283 ms, Bazett QTc 386 ms. Sinus rhythm at about 62-63 bpm with an upright P wave before each conducted QRS (P-R about 198 ms, borderline) interrupted by one premature beat and a compensatory pause; no atrial fibrillation is present on this tracing. Only ECG in the chart - her paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented by diagnosis, not on this recording.

Regular rhythm at about 70 bpm with a consistent atrial deflection before every QRS (P-R 144 ms) - sinus in origin, but recorded with a reversed limb-lead pattern: P and QRS are inverted in leads I and II with a positive aVR, giving a measured frontal axis of about -173 degrees (extreme axis deviation), while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression. Sinus rhythm at about 70 bpm, P-R 164 ms, QRS 90 ms, frontal axis +40 degrees, no bundle branch block. Sinus rhythm at about 68 bpm with a uniform upright P wave, P-R 146 ms, QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +33 to +66 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart; it satisfies the ECG required after the 2/12/2026 escitalopram start.

Sinus rhythm with frequent premature atrial complexes producing alternating long and short cycles (RR 416-1168 ms, mean rate about 66 bpm); every QRS is preceded by an upright P wave in lead II with P-R about 176 ms, so the rhythm is not atrial fibrillation. Sinus rhythm at about 70 bpm, P-R 128 ms, QRS 86 ms, axis +45 degrees, no bundle branch block. Relevant because escitalopram has been taken continuously since 5/2024 (see QT safety item).

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 141 bpm (RR 404-454 ms). The prior ECG of 7/11/2022 showed irregularly irregular atrial fibrillation at about 107 bpm, so the organised flutter is new and the fibrillation has resolved; atrial flutter was coded at this admission. QTc is unchanged (431 to 416 ms).

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 492-500 ms), with a P wave before each QRS and P-R 138 ms. QRS is narrow (58 ms), frontal axis +69 degrees (normal), no conduction abnormality. QT 277 ms with Bazett QTc 392 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at about 102 bpm, P-R 152 ms, QRS 70 ms, axis +59 degrees, no bundle branch block, QT 308 ms and QTc 400 ms. Sinus bradycardia at about 52 bpm (RR 1145-1180 ms) with a uniform upright P wave before every QRS, P-R 180 ms (upper normal), QRS 68 ms, axis +36 degrees, no block. QT 413 ms, QTc 384 ms. Sinus tachycardia at about 122 bpm, P-R 126 ms, QRS 102 ms with only a small terminal r' in V1 (incomplete right bundle pattern, duration below 120 ms). The earlier tracing from the same day (1:33, record 106516875) showed complete right bundle branch block with QRS 144 ms and a broad terminal R in V1; the QRS has narrowed to 102 ms, i.e. the bundle branch block has resolved. QTc is essentially unchanged (462 to 416 ms).

Sinus rhythm at about 62-64 bpm with a low-amplitude but constant P wave (P-R 170 ms) and one late ectopic beat. QRS 90 ms, axis +66 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is broad and late (peak ~410 ms): QT about 540 ms and Bazett QTc about 549 ms, markedly prolonged on amiodarone started 11/10/2025. The prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (sinus with marked pauses, QTc about 438 ms) shows the QTc has risen by more than 100 ms - see the QT safety item.

Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR 408-726 ms) with no discernible P wave in any lead, only low-amplitude fibrillatory activity, so no PR interval can be measured. This is the only ECG in the chart; the patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026, i.e. after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days - by 4/24/2026. Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days (by 8/24/2026). Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started (re-started as an outpatient, the December 2025 order having been an inpatient course) at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days - by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, well before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since; the requirement is overdue as of the evaluation date.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been recorded since 3/9/2025, but the window has not closed as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation, so the requirement is not yet due; it should be arranged in the next five days.

Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the follow-up requirement was completed on time.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded 8/22/2025 and carried in every cardiology clinic note). Current medications are levothyroxine only - no anticoagulant and no antiplatelet; no anticoagulant order has ever been written. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1, coronary atherosclerosis/vascular disease = 1), which is well above the threshold at which the 2023 AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. The 2025 procedure-related haemorrhage was a single peri-procedural event and is not documented as an ongoing contraindication.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (acting under the clinic standing order, which permits pharmacist dose adjustment) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. The 3/1/2026 memo requires a clinic INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026 and no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the required follow-up is overdue in a 95-year-old on amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin.

48-year-old man whose cardiology clinic notes consistently list paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (most recently 8/4/2026). Warfarin/heparin were given only during the February and June 2025 admissions; current clinic medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline, so no anticoagulant is current. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure documented 2/26/2025 and hypertension), and with a score of >=2 in a man the guideline recommends oral anticoagulation.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the March 2025 admission for embolic cerebral infarction. Current clinic medications are famotidine, metoprolol and levothyroxine - rate control only, with no anticoagulant on the list at any visit since (last visit 6/2/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (prior cerebral infarction = 2, age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1, female = 1). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention; documented falls and thrombocytopenia should be weighed but are not an absolute contraindication.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 8/20/2026 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nevertheless listed as a current medication and re-prescribed (order 8/20/2026, valid to 1/4/2027), together with aspirin and clopidogrel. Restarting a DOAC plus dual antiplatelet therapy after a recent major GI bleed has not been reconciled with the documented hold and requires prescriber review.

At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-issued the same day (valid to 1/3/2027) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid to 12/23/2026), and the note's medication list contains both. Both orders are still current on 9/24/2026, so the patient is prescribed two oral anticoagulants simultaneously (plus clopidogrel) - a bleeding hazard that needs immediate reconciliation.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (17:13 record 107914094 and 19:36 record 103088543) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at about 135-145 bpm with no organised P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and atrial fibrillation was coded at that encounter. The rhythm statement in the note is contradicted by the same-day tracings and should be corrected.

Sinus rhythm at about 102 bpm, P-R 152 ms, QRS 70 ms, axis +59 degrees, no bundle branch block, QT 308 ms and QTc 400 ms. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive heart failure documented 2/26/2025 and hypertension), and with a score of >=2 in a man the guideline recommends oral anticoagulation.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the March 2025 admission for embolic cerebral infarction. Current clinic medications are famotidine, metoprolol and levothyroxine - rate control only, with no anticoagulant on the list at any visit since (last visit 6/2/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (prior cerebral infarction = 2, age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1, female = 1). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention; documented falls and thrombocytopenia should be weighed but are not an absolute contraindication.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 8/20/2026 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nevertheless listed as a current medication and re-prescribed (order 8/20/2026, valid to 1/4/2027), together with aspirin and clopidogrel. Restarting a DOAC plus dual antiplatelet therapy after a recent major GI bleed has not been reconciled with the documented hold and requires prescriber review.

At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-issued the same day (valid to 1/3/2027) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid to 12/23/2026), and the note's medication list contains both. Both orders are still current on 9/24/2026, so the patient is prescribed two oral anticoagulants simultaneously (plus clopidogrel) - a bleeding hazard that needs immediate reconciliation.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (17:13 record 107914094 and 19:36 record 103088543) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at about 135-145 bpm with no organised P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - and atrial fibrillation was coded at that encounter. The rhythm statement in the note is contradicted by the same-day tracings and should be corrected.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is current (re-ordered 7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027). His most recent ECG, 11/24/2025, shows sinus rhythm at 62-64 bpm with QT about 540 ms and Bazett QTc about 549 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which under the clinic QT monitoring memo requires prescriber review. Electrolytes are not contributory (K 4.3 mEq/L and Mg 2.1 mg/dL on 6/9/2026). No repeat ECG has been obtained since amiodarone was continued.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027) and warfarin. Her most recent ECG in the chart (4/27/2022, record 101515306) shows atrial fibrillation at about 74-77 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT (~555-580 ms, Bazett QTc ~616-640 ms), far above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT memo, so prescriber review is required. Latest electrolytes 6/17/2026: K 4.2 mEq/L, Mg 1.9 mg/dL. A current ECG should be obtained as part of that review.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with an upright, uniform P wave before every QRS (P-R 182 ms). Narrow QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about +47 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 319 ms, Bazett QTc 370 ms - normal despite citalopram 40 mg daily. No earlier ECG is available for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at about 104 bpm, regular, with a low-amplitude P wave and P-R 120 ms. QRS 92 ms, axis +38 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 366 ms, Bazett QTc 480 ms (upper normal). Compared with 6/20/2025 (sinus tachycardia 147 bpm, P-R 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 434 ms) the rate has fallen; there is no new arrhythmia or block and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at about 108 bpm with a P wave before every QRS, P-R 114 ms, QRS 88 ms, frontal axis +36 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 343 ms, Bazett QTc 463 ms (borderline but below 500 ms). Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR (348-650 ms), mean rate about 136 bpm, no organised P waves (only a negative baseline undulation in lead II), so no measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, axis about 0 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 282 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms. The ECG two hours earlier the same day (107914094) shows the same atrial fibrillation at 134 bpm with QTc 439 ms, so nothing has changed between them - but both contradict the 6/10/2026 note describing sinus rhythm at 72 (see contradiction item).

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at about 69-72 bpm (RR 864-882 ms) with no P wave visible in any lead on beat-by-beat or signal-averaged review, only a small negative deflection in lead II - an accelerated junctional / low atrial rhythm rather than sinus, and no PR interval can be measured. One late premature beat. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about -24 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 405 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 also lacked sinus P waves (rate 61, QTc about 401 ms), so the rhythm and intervals are unchanged; note that tracing also showed a reversed limb-lead pattern.

Sinus rhythm at about 98 bpm, regular, P-R 110 ms, QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about +4 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 301 ms, Bazett QTc 384 ms. Single ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at about 72 bpm with a constant upright P wave, P-R 142 ms, QRS 76 ms, axis +22 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave ends early (peak ~270 ms): QT about 376 ms, Bazett QTc about 412 ms - normal. Only ECG in the chart; it predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026, so it cannot serve as the post-start tracing (see follow-up item).

Atrial fibrillation: grossly irregular RR intervals (462-1154 ms), mean ventricular rate about 70 bpm, no consistent P waves, so no PR interval. QRS 78 ms, axis +27 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 421 ms with Bazett QTc about 491 ms. Three days earlier (11/12/2024, record 107873952) the rhythm was regular sinus at 69 bpm with clear P waves (P-R 166 ms) and QTc 398 ms, so this tracing shows new atrial fibrillation and a QTc rise of more than 60 ms. She is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus bradycardia at about 58 bpm with prominent upright P waves, P-R 106 ms, QRS 80 ms, axis +62 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 420 ms, Bazett QTc 414 ms. Essentially identical to the tracing of the previous day (106045460: 62 bpm, P-R 110 ms, QTc 440 ms) - no rhythm, conduction or QTc change. This is the baseline against which the ECG now due after the 9/15/2026 haloperidol start should be compared.
Sinus rhythm at about 83 bpm, very regular, P-R 140 ms, QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 346 ms, Bazett QTc 407 ms. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at about 76 bpm with large upright P waves, P-R 152 ms, QRS 66 ms, axis +64 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 399 ms, Bazett QTc 451 ms. Compared with 2/2/2020 (sinus 75 bpm, P-R 150 ms, QTc about 499 ms) the QTc is slightly shorter (change under 60 ms) and there is no new arrhythmia or block.

Sinus tachycardia at about 120 bpm with consistent P waves, P-R 178 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis +51 degrees, no conduction block. QT 274 ms, QTc 388 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus at 108 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 393 ms) there is no significant change: no new arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and QTc differs by only 5 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at about 55 bpm (RR 1074-1118 ms). Each QRS is preceded by a broad upright P wave with a prolonged P-R of about 216-230 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms with prominent septal q waves, frontal axis about 0 to +60 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 396 ms, Bazett QTc 377 ms. The prior ECG of 11/30/2024 showed sinus rhythm with frequent bigeminal ectopy, P-R about 190 ms and QTc about 411 ms; the rhythm is still sinus, there is no new bundle branch block and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR (316-602 ms), mean rate about 147 bpm, no organised atrial activity and no measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about -21 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 260 ms, Bazett QTc 413 ms. The tracing of the previous evening (107374881) was also irregular without consistent P waves at a slower rate (about 84 bpm), so atrial fibrillation is not new between these two; he is on apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at about 72 bpm with a well-formed upright P wave, P-R 166 ms, QRS 86 ms (narrow - the apparent widening on automated review was baseline offset), frontal axis about +12 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT about 353 ms and Bazett QTc about 391 ms. On 11/21/2025 the T wave was much later (peak 385 ms) with QT about 481 ms and QTc about 512 ms, so the QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms; the rhythm remains sinus, consistent with the 11/23/2025 note.

Sinus rhythm at about 74-75 bpm with a uniform upright P wave, P-R 182 ms (upper normal), QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 372 ms, Bazett QTc 413 ms. One late ectopic beat. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at about 112 bpm, regular (RR 536-542 ms), with a P wave before every QRS and P-R 168 ms. QRS 76 ms, frontal axis +34 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 283 ms, Bazett QTc 386 ms. The prior ECG of 7/4/2022 was also sinus at 115 bpm with P-R 160 ms and QTc 389 ms - unchanged. Note this 2023 tracing is the most recent available even though atrial flutter was coded in 9/2025, and he remains on apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at about 62-63 bpm with an upright P wave before each conducted QRS (P-R about 198 ms, borderline) interrupted by one premature beat and a compensatory pause; no atrial fibrillation is present on this tracing. QRS 98 ms, frontal axis about -30 degrees, reported as left axis deviation (lead I positive, lead II nearly isoelectric, III and aVF negative). No bundle branch block. QT 390 ms, Bazett QTc 397 ms. Only ECG in the chart - her paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented by diagnosis, not on this recording.

Regular rhythm at about 70 bpm with a consistent atrial deflection before every QRS (P-R 144 ms) - sinus in origin, but recorded with a reversed limb-lead pattern: P and QRS are inverted in leads I and II with a positive aVR, giving a measured frontal axis of about -173 degrees (extreme axis deviation), while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block. QT 350 ms, Bazett QTc 377 ms - normal on escitalopram. Only ECG in the chart; it was obtained 19 days after the escitalopram start (see follow-up item).

Sinus rhythm at about 70 bpm, P-R 164 ms, QRS 90 ms, frontal axis +40 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is late and broad (peak ~365 ms) giving QT about 487 ms and Bazett QTc about 527 ms - prolonged. The prior ECG of 6/17/2020 (sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, QTc about 448 ms) shows an increase in QTc of more than 60 ms. She remains on citalopram 40 mg daily (see QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at about 68 bpm with a uniform upright P wave, P-R 146 ms, QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +33 to +66 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. T waves are inverted in leads I and V2 with a slow return to baseline; QT about 434 ms giving Bazett QTc about 463 ms - borderline but below 500 ms. Only ECG in the chart; it satisfies the ECG required after the 2/12/2026 escitalopram start.

Sinus rhythm with frequent premature atrial complexes producing alternating long and short cycles (RR 416-1168 ms, mean rate about 66 bpm); every QRS is preceded by an upright P wave in lead II with P-R about 176 ms, so the rhythm is not atrial fibrillation. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about -5 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT 378 ms, Bazett QTc about 358-397 ms depending on the cycle used. The prior ECG of 12/13/2018 was regular sinus at 66 bpm with P-R 200 ms and QTc about 386 ms - no new arrhythmia, block or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at about 70 bpm, P-R 128 ms, QRS 86 ms, axis +45 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is markedly late (T peak ~375 ms) giving QT about 492 ms and Bazett QTc about 524 ms - prolonged. The previous ECG of 11/23/2022 had QTc 347 ms, so QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. Relevant because escitalopram has been taken continuously since 5/2024 (see QT safety item).

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 141 bpm (RR 404-454 ms). Signal-averaged analysis of the inter-QRS segments shows organised atrial activity at about 282 per minute - exactly twice the ventricular rate - with two identical atrial deflections per cycle in leads II, III and V1, i.e. atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction; no true PR interval can be assigned. QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +1 degree, no bundle branch block. QT 271 ms, Bazett QTc 416 ms. The prior ECG of 7/11/2022 showed irregularly irregular atrial fibrillation at about 107 bpm, so the organised flutter is new and the fibrillation has resolved; atrial flutter was coded at this admission. QTc is unchanged (431 to 416 ms).

Sinus rhythm at about 82 bpm, regular, with a clear upright P wave, P-R 158 ms, QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about +34 degrees, no conduction abnormality. QT 370 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at about 91 bpm with an upright P wave in lead II beginning about 210 ms before the QRS (P-R about 175 ms, within normal limits once the depressed PR segment is excluded), QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about -17 to +45 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms. The prior ECG of 5/16/2021 was sinus at 87 bpm with P-R 142 ms and QTc 390 ms - no new arrhythmia, conduction block or significant QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 492-500 ms), with a P wave before each QRS and P-R 138 ms. QRS is narrow (58 ms), frontal axis +69 degrees (normal), no conduction abnormality. QT 277 ms with Bazett QTc 392 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at about 102 bpm, P-R 152 ms, QRS 70 ms, axis +59 degrees, no bundle branch block, QT 308 ms and QTc 400 ms. The comparison tracing was taken one minute earlier the same day (8/23/2021) and is essentially identical (rate 100, P-R 150 ms, QRS 70 ms, QTc 397 ms): no interval or rhythm change.

Sinus bradycardia at about 52 bpm (RR 1145-1180 ms) with a uniform upright P wave before every QRS, P-R 180 ms (upper normal), QRS 68 ms, axis +36 degrees, no block. QT 413 ms, QTc 384 ms. Versus 5/22/2023 (sinus at 58 bpm with occasional ectopy, P-R 148 ms, QTc 379 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no new bundle branch block and no significant QTc change; the patient remains in sinus rhythm on warfarin for atrial fibrillation.

Sinus tachycardia at about 122 bpm, P-R 126 ms, QRS 102 ms with only a small terminal r' in V1 (incomplete right bundle pattern, duration below 120 ms). Frontal axis about +135 degrees - right axis deviation (S dominant in lead I, positive in III/aVF). QT 293 ms, QTc 416 ms. The earlier tracing from the same day (1:33, record 106516875) showed complete right bundle branch block with QRS 144 ms and a broad terminal R in V1; the QRS has narrowed to 102 ms, i.e. the bundle branch block has resolved. QTc is essentially unchanged (462 to 416 ms).

Sinus rhythm at about 62-64 bpm with a low-amplitude but constant P wave (P-R 170 ms) and one late ectopic beat. QRS 90 ms, axis +66 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is broad and late (peak ~410 ms): QT about 540 ms and Bazett QTc about 549 ms, markedly prolonged on amiodarone started 11/10/2025. The prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (sinus with marked pauses, QTc about 438 ms) shows the QTc has risen by more than 100 ms - see the QT safety item.

Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR 408-726 ms) with no discernible P wave in any lead, only low-amplitude fibrillatory activity, so no PR interval can be measured. Mean ventricular rate about 109 bpm. QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about -47 degrees (left axis deviation), no bundle branch block. QT 313 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart; the patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (e.g. 9/12/2025 and 6/22/2026). No anticoagulant is current: the only active clinic prescriptions are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin; the DOACs she received (dabigatran/rivaroxaban/apixaban) ended with the January 2025 admission. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (age >=75 = 2, female = 1, hypertension, heart failure, diabetes, prior cerebral infarction = 2, coronary/vascular disease), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. Aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily has been continuous since 5/14/2024 and is current (order 7/18/2026, valid to 12/26/2026). The most recent ECG in the chart (10/8/2023, record 108018814) shows sinus rhythm at 68-70 bpm with QT about 492 ms and Bazett QTc about 524 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT memo, despite the 5/14/2024 note describing that tracing as 'QT acceptable'. Latest electrolytes 3/18/2026: K 3.8 mEq/L, Mg 1.9 mg/dL. Prescriber review (and a current ECG) is required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (twice the dose recommended above age 60 in other guidance, and a QT watch-list drug) is current - order 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027. Her most recent ECG, 11/10/2023 (record 104821039), shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT about 487 ms and Bazett QTc about 527 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which requires prescriber review under the clinic QT memo. Most recent electrolytes: K 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and Mg 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025).

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025. Because the start was on or after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days (by 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met - although that tracing shows QTc ~549 ms and is the basis of a separate QT safety item.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days (by 3/16/2026). ECG 104882441 was obtained on 3/7/2026, five days after the start, and shows sinus rhythm with QTc ~370 ms, so the requirement was completed in time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (ECG due by 3/14/2026). ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start (QTc ~460 ms), so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026, i.e. after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days - by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded on 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start, so the requirement was not met within the required time and remains outstanding past its due date. Escitalopram has been continued (current order 8/11/2026); the 4/29/2026 tracing itself showed QTc ~377 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days (by 8/24/2026). No ECG exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested by fax and not yet received. That outside tracing, if obtained on 8/18/2026, would have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started (re-started as an outpatient, the December 2025 order having been an inpatient course) at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days - by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, well before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since; the requirement is overdue as of the evaluation date.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been recorded since 3/9/2025, but the window has not closed as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation, so the requirement is not yet due; it should be arranged in the next five days.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 9/1/2026 the physician documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the follow-up requirement was completed on time.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded 8/22/2025 and carried in every cardiology clinic note). Current medications are levothyroxine only - no anticoagulant and no antiplatelet; no anticoagulant order has ever been written. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1, coronary atherosclerosis/vascular disease = 1), which is well above the threshold at which the 2023 AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. The 2025 procedure-related haemorrhage was a single peri-procedural event and is not documented as an ongoing contraindication.

The 3/1/2026 memo requires a clinic INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026 and no INR has been drawn since the dose change, so the required follow-up is overdue in a 95-year-old on amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin.
